text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Protesters march in Hong Kong: Democracy activists heartened by China's hands-off stand as nothing done to stop demonstration.
- Canada Day no longer July 1 at many firms: CAW started long-weekend trend that calls for working on the holiday.
- Unhappy Russian workers threaten nuclear disaster: Unpaid wages trigger protest, possible submarine sabotage.
- Armchair travellers set for trip to Mars: Pathfinder's images of Red Planet will be transmitted live from surface.
- Waves of arrivals shape broad Spadina: Communities come and go on grand old street in Toronto that is so rich in character some people worry about the tourism deterrent.
- U.S. economy gearing down: Amid factories' slowdown and construction's slump, Fed expected to hold steady on rates.
- Nike's hockey plans put Bauer on thin ice: Closing of Cambridge plant could spell end of skate maker's Canadian presence.
- Gulf's gunslinger kicks up the dust: J.P. Bryan - oil firm boss, Wild West buff and outsider by nature - is in no mood to mend fences.
- Berlin comes in from the cold: The divided city was too risky for builders. Now united, it is such a magnet that one developer sees 'conspicuous overbuilding.'
- U.S. equity deals turn risky: Canadian companies find cross-border financings can be a gamble. Several recent issues have fallen short of target of have been cancelled.
- Viacom wants USA Networks auction to settle Seagram fight.
- New Kmart Canada chief seeking niche.
